transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Mbeki, thank you for coming in. I asked to see you today because I found a mistake in how we handled your son's developmental screening referral.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I see.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Essentially, after you missed that first appointment, the referral was marked as completed in our computer system. Because of that, we didn't actually follow up to reschedule it, so the screening never happened. Does that make sense, or should I explain that differently?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It makes sense.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry for any confusion this has caused. We have been incredibly shorthanded in the clinic lately, and it looks like the process just broke down.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I missed the appointment because I couldn't get a sitter. I thought you would call.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can hear how frustrating that is. You were counting on us to reach out so you could manage your work schedule and your childcare, and we let you down.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is just a lot of time off work.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Exactly. It's not just about the appointment, it's about the impact on your business and your finances when you have to rearrange your entire day. I really recognize how stressful that pressure is for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Does that explanation of the error clear everything up for you, or do you have any questions about how it happened?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No, I think I understand.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Now, we need to get this sorted.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I hope it's not too late for the boy.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: But I have to go in a few minutes for a procedure, so let's wrap up quickly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just get this rescheduled.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll have my team look into it. We'll probably send some kind of email or something.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't always check my email during the work day.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll see. Just stay tuned for a notification.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I would rather just have a date.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right, but like I said, I'm running late. We'll figure out the timing and get back to you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just don't want to miss more work for nothing.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I get that, but we'll just have to wait and see what the clinic says. I'll try to make sure it happens.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Alright, we're all set here. I'll be in touch.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('wrap up quickly', 'running late') and dismisses the patient's concerns to leave for a procedure.

E.justification: The error is named in the first turn, lay language is used, and comprehension is checked twice ('Does that make sense', 'Does that explanation... clear everything up').

A.justification: A direct apology is offered, but it is immediately diluted by an excuse regarding being 'incredibly shorthanded in the clinic'.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('frustrating', 'stressful') and references the patient's specific concerns regarding childcare and finances.

T.justification: The resident provides only placeholders ('we'll see', 'stay tuned', 'we'll figure it out') with no specific timeline or prevention plan.
